paper_title: Shuttle Between the Instructions and the Parameters of Large Language   Models
caption: : The induction performance of SHIP and SFT on SNI with respect to the number of observed samples. The accuracy is the average accuracy over all seen and unseen tasks.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the induction performance of two methods—SHIP and vanilla SFT—on the SNI benchmark, measured by accuracy as a function of the number of observed samples, ranging from 1 to 6. The x-axis, labeled "observed samples," is linear and integer-valued, with tick marks at each integer from 1 to 6. The y-axis, labeled "accuracy," is also linear, ranging from 0.3 to 0.8, with tick marks at 0.1 intervals. The green line with circular markers represents SHIP, which starts at an accuracy of approximately 0.81 at 1 observed sample, remains relatively stable around 0.80 through 3 samples, dips slightly to about 0.78 at 4 samples, and then gradually increases to approximately 0.81 at 6 samples. The blue line with circular markers represents vanilla SFT, which begins at an accuracy of about 0.34 at 1 sample, increases slightly to around 0.37 at 2 samples, remains flat until 4 samples, then rises to approximately 0.40 at 5 samples and reaches about 0.45 at 6 samples. The plot includes a legend in the lower right corner identifying the two methods.
